# Maskin

> The open-source, MCP-native system where your whole team — humans and AI agents — closes the loop together, from customer signal to shipped bet to measured outcome, with shared memory and a real process. Think of it as the default system for setting up agentic teams: connect Claude (or any MCP client) and drive the workspace directly.

Maskin gives humans and AI agents one shared place to work. Everything flows through a single pipeline — **Insights → Bets → Tasks** — that people and agents read and write together, so context compounds instead of getting lost in scattered chat histories. Maskin is MCP-native and API-first: the UI, agents, and your Claude client all drive the same HTTP surface, and the MCP tools are a thin layer over it.

Run it two ways: **self-hosted** (one `docker-compose` file, free under Apache 2.0) or **managed**. Bring your own model key (Anthropic, OpenAI, or local via Ollama).

Setup in one line — connect Claude to a Maskin instance over MCP, then ask Claude to call `get_started`:
`claude mcp add maskin --transport http --url https://<your-maskin-host>/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer <MASKIN_API_KEY>" --header "X-Workspace-Id: <WORKSPACE_ID>"`

## Top pages

- [Maskin homepage](https://maskin.io/): The product pitch — what Maskin is, how the closed loop from insight to shipped bet works, and the two ways to run it (self-hosted, managed).
- [MCP server](https://maskin.io/mcp-server): The Maskin MCP server — the tool surface Claude and other MCP-native agents use to drive a Maskin workspace over HTTP or stdio.
- [Alternatives](https://maskin.io/alternatives/open-source-jira-alternative/): Head-to-head comparisons with existing tools — currently the open-source Jira alternative, more comparison pages landing on the same path.

## Articles

- [What is an agentic workspace?](https://maskin.io/docs/what-is-an-agentic-workspace/): The category Maskin is built around — a shared surface where humans and AI agents work on the same typed objects, and the closed loop (insight → bet → task → shipped → repeat) that defines it.
- [What is MCP-native?](https://maskin.io/docs/what-is-mcp-native/): The Model Context Protocol and why Maskin is built around it — MCP-native means the protocol is the substrate, not an afterthought, and makes bring-your-own-model real. Part of the agentic-workspace cluster (what-is-an-agentic-workspace, ai-product-management-tool, bet-based-product-planning).
- [MCP-native workspace: a category, not a checkbox](https://maskin.io/docs/mcp-native-workspace/): The category above individual MCP servers — a shared, typed object graph where the entire product surface is exposed to agents through MCP. Four architectural markers separate it from an app-with-an-MCP-integration, plus the marketplace-vs-category and AI21-sandbox-workspace disambiguations. Companion to the what-is-mcp-native cornerstone.
- [What is a stateful orchestration substrate?](https://maskin.io/docs/what-is-a-stateful-orchestration-substrate/): The shared, typed store that carries state between stateless AI agents so a pipeline produces coherent work across handoffs. Names handoff amnesia as an architectural failure mode (LongRCA Bench: top diagnostic tools score 13.2% root-step accuracy on long-horizon runs), catalogues five independent August-2026 sources converging on the same fix pattern (RedHat, Recuris, Empirical, ZS Associates, DEV Community), and frames Maskin's typed-object graph as one shape of the substrate. Part of the agentic-workspace cluster.
- [Agent observability: when the workspace is the trace](https://maskin.io/docs/agent-observability/): Agent observability is the discipline of tracing, evaluating, and monitoring what an AI agent does across a multi-step task — a tier above LLM observability where the trace unit is a task with tool calls and decisions rather than a single model call. The load-bearing frame the definitional SERP does not name: a typed workspace graph IS the agent-level trace, so the audit trail is a side effect of the work rather than a separate telemetry pipeline. Covers the LLM-obs-vs-agent-obs vocabulary bridge, the three-layer stack (model tier / loop tier / substrate tier), continuous eval-as-a-loop as the wedge past Anthropic's pre-deploy framing, and the current OSS tools (Langfuse, Arize Phoenix, LangSmith, OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions). Part of the agentic-workspace cluster.
- [Ambient agent workspace: the workspace-graph is the fifth post-chat pattern](https://maskin.io/docs/ambient-agent-workspace/): Chat breaks around 30 seconds and background/ambient AI needs push, not pull. Names workspace-graph-as-inbox as the fifth pattern alongside Adaline's four (verb surface, generative canvas, delegated agent, ambient capture) and LangChain's Agent Inbox, with the four failure modes ambient agents share and how a typed object graph carries state across many parallel loops. Part of the agentic-workspace cluster.
- [What is an Agent Inbox? (LangChain's ambient-agent UX pattern)](https://maskin.io/docs/agent-inbox/): Harrison Chase's definitional post at LangChain (Jan 2025) named the Agent Inbox as the UX for ambient agents — a queue where the agent posts three interrupt types to a human (notify, question, review) instead of running a chat. Definitional citations, the LangGraph open-source reference UI, the Superhuman shipped example, and when the flat queue starts to buckle in favor of the workspace-graph. Tail companion to the ambient-agent-workspace cornerstone.
- [Human in the loop AI: when it's real, when it's theater](https://maskin.io/docs/learn/human-in-the-loop-ai/): "In the loop" doesn't guarantee real oversight. Override rate is the honest metric — 0% is rubber-stamping, above 20% is a broken model, real HITL sits in the middle band watched over time. Distinguishes HITL from human-on-the-loop (HOTL), explains why EU AI Act Article 14 does not mandate HITL by name (it requires effective oversight — understand, monitor, intervene, halt), and argues for a tiered approval policy enforced at the governance layer, not inside agent code. Pairs with the ambient-agent-workspace piece on the HOTL vocabulary.
- [The three tiers of AI-native work — the closure diagnostic](https://maskin.io/docs/three-tiers-ai-native-work/): The tier-comparison hub above the trilogy. Sorts the AI-native tool landscape by object of work and the event that closes the loop — coding agents on a merged PR, task trackers with AI summaries on a status change, knowledge spaces on a page view — and names the closure diagnostic that separates artifact-closing tools from outcome-closing tools. Frames the agentic workspace as a fourth tier where the object of work is a shaped bet with a win condition and the terminal event is a validated outcome. Interlinks to all three tier spokes (ai-product-workspace-vs-coding-agent, ai-product-management-tool, agentic-workspace-vs-knowledge-space) and the cornerstone; preempts the false-closure vocabulary collision with agent-lifecycle-framework research.
- [The closed-loop workspace: what tier 4 of AI-native work actually is](https://maskin.io/docs/closed-loop-workspace/): The affirmative fourth spoke of the three-tiers trilogy — the tier whose object of work is a shaped bet with a win condition and whose terminal event is a shipped change measured against that condition. Runs the closure diagnostic in the affirmative direction, names the object-model / terminal-event / human-split requirements, and disambiguates from the two OSS "closed-loop" shapes already shipping under the same name (Closedloop.ai for SDLC scope, Maskin for broader knowledge work). Diagnostic-frame companion to the what-is-an-agentic-workspace cornerstone.
- [AI product management tool: the loop, not a tracker](https://maskin.io/docs/ai-product-management-tool/): Why an AI product management tool should close the loop between learning and shipping — insight becomes a testable bet, owned jointly by humans and agents — instead of bolting summaries onto a task tracker.
- [AI product workspace vs AI coding agent](https://maskin.io/docs/ai-product-workspace-vs-coding-agent/): Two agentic tiers, not competitors. A coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, plus the eleven open-source control planes shipped Feb–Aug 2026) terminates on a merged PR; an AI product workspace terminates on a validated outcome against a shaped bet's win condition. Self-hosting, MCP, and approval queues are now table stakes on both tiers — the honest differentiator is the object model beneath the dashboard. Most teams that ship software will run both. The third leg of the tier-comparison cluster alongside the tracker-tier (ai-product-management-tool) and notes-tier (agentic-workspace-vs-knowledge-space) companions.
- [Agentic workspace vs knowledge space: why Obsidian, Mem, and Confluence stop before the bet](https://maskin.io/docs/agentic-workspace-vs-knowledge-space/): The tier-3 leg of the three-tiers trilogy — knowledge spaces (Obsidian, Mem, Confluence, Raft) own capture and retrieval; the failure mode is closure, not retrieval. The closure diagnostic that separates a tracker-with-narrator from an agentic workspace generalises cleanly to the notes tier: a note without a win condition cannot close a loop on an outcome. Includes the tier-3 comparison spine and the honest case for running both.
- [Agent skills vs MCP vs cursor rules vs workflows: what each layer solves](https://maskin.io/docs/agent-skills-vs-mcp-vs-cursor-rules-vs-workflows/): The `agent skills vs MCP` SERP debate is a category mistake. Four different layers — MCP is what an agent can reach (protocol), skills are what it invokes (packaged capability), Cursor rules / AGENTS.md are how it acts (behavioral directives), workflows are who runs when (orchestration). Includes the four-way comparison table, the concrete refund-a-subscription example that ships all four, and the unclaimed anti-frame: skills that fire against typed workspace state rather than a git repo. Part of the agentic-workspace cluster.
- [Bet-based product planning: the anti-backlog doctrine](https://maskin.io/docs/bet-based-product-planning/): Shape Up's anti-backlog doctrine, run as a live loop — plan in shaped bets with a win condition instead of a growing queue of tickets, with the bet a machine-readable object owned jointly by humans and agents.
- [How to run bet-based planning: the four-step loop](https://maskin.io/docs/how-to-run-bet-based-planning/): The four repeatable steps for running bet-based planning — shape a bet from raw insight, give it a win condition, run a fixed-size cycle, and close the loop on validation. The how-to companion to the bet-based-product-planning anchor.
- [How to build an AI SDR loop in Maskin (MCP + Unipile, HITL approval on outbound)](https://maskin.io/docs/how-to-build-ai-sdr-loop/): Seven-step build guide for running an AI SDR loop on Maskin's typed object graph — signal, research, draft, human approval, send via a sender-lane MCP (Unipile for LinkedIn, Postmark/Resend for email), reply routing, close condition. Human-on-the-loop with override rate as the honest metric. The concrete build companion to the open-source-ai-sdr alternatives map.
- [Bet vs backlog: do you want a queue or a loop?](https://maskin.io/docs/bet-vs-backlog/): The head-to-head — a backlog is a queue of tickets that decays into aspiration, a bet is a time-bounded, falsifiable commitment with a win condition run on a fixed cycle. Maskin makes the bet a machine-readable object the loop can actually run on. Part of the bet-based-planning cluster.
- [Self-hosted AI workspace: bring your own model](https://maskin.io/docs/self-hosted-ai-workspace/): Maskin is fully self-hostable under Apache 2.0 with bring-your-own-model — run the closed loop on your own infrastructure with Claude, Codex, or a local model. An open-source alternative to Claude Cowork, Codex, or ChatGPT workspaces. Part of the agentic-workspace cluster (what-is-an-agentic-workspace, ai-product-management-tool, what-is-mcp-native).
- [Open source Jira alternative that actually closes the loop](https://maskin.io/alternatives/open-source-jira-alternative/): Plane, OpenProject, and Taiga are open-source Jira alternatives that keep the ticket-and-backlog model. Maskin is Apache 2.0, MCP-native, and replaces the ticket with a bet — a testable hypothesis owned jointly by humans and agents — so the loop from signal to shipped, validated outcome actually closes. Part of the agentic-workspace cluster.
- [Open source Notion alternative for AI product management](https://maskin.io/alternatives/open-source-notion-alternative/): AppFlowy, AFFiNE, Anytype, Docmost, and Outline are open-source Notion clones that preserve the page-and-database object model — and Notion's own 2026 pivot (Custom Agents Feb 2026, Developer Platform May 2026) still bolts the AI onto pages. Maskin replaces the page with a bet — a testable hypothesis with a win condition, jointly owned by humans and agents — so the AI product management loop actually closes. Apache 2.0, MCP-native, self-hostable. Companion to the Jira alt on the /alternatives/ comparison cluster.
- [Open source AI SDR: the six real repos and the loop shape that works](https://maskin.io/alternatives/open-source-ai-sdr/): The honest map of the six OSS AI SDR repos on GitHub in 2026 (MatthewDailey/open-sdr, OpenOutreach, ZeroGTM, Signal, personizeai/revenue-os, kandksolvefast/ai-sdr-agent), the $50-200/mo vs $2k-5k/mo cost split between OSS and closed SaaS (11x, Artisan, Qualified, SalesForge, AiSDR), and the human-on-the-loop shape that makes outbound work instead of getting your domain blacklisted. Companion to the how-to-build-ai-sdr-loop build guide.
- [Open source Codex alternative — closed-loop knowledge-work workspace](https://maskin.io/alternatives/open-source-alternative-to-codex/): OpenAI Codex's terminal event is a merged PR; Maskin's is an outcome validated against a shaped bet's win condition. Apache 2.0, MCP-native, self-hostable, model-agnostic at the MCP protocol layer — so Codex, Claude, a local model, or a fine-tune all run inside the same workspace. Written for the OpenAI-side buyer whose loop is "ship a decision," not "close a coding ticket." Codex-shaped coding work still runs; the loop past the merge is the extension. Companion to the Claude Cowork alt (mirrors the same argument for the Anthropic-side buyer).
- [Self-hosted AI agent control plane for knowledge work (not coding tasks)](https://maskin.io/alternatives/self-hosted-ai-agent-control-plane/): Twelve open-source self-hosted control planes shipped Feb-Aug 2026 (amux, Crewship, Preloop, Nora, Musematic, Mission Control, Clawix, Vornik, Zoink, herdctl, danrex/fleet, VNX) — all Docker/Podman/K8s, approval-first, most MCP-native, and all built around the same object model: a kanban of coding tasks that closes when a PR merges. Maskin sits in the same category on the four table-stakes commodities (Apache-2.0, self-hostable, MCP-native, approval-first) but diverges on the object model — loop on typed objects (insight → bet → task → validated) rather than a kanban of coding tasks. Includes Van Deth's solopreneur/chat-as-primary counter-frame as the honest challenge at n=1 scale. Category-vocabulary page on the /alternatives/ cluster.
- [Self-hosted AI agents — the 2026 OSS landscape, honestly categorised](https://maskin.io/alternatives/self-hosted-ai-agents/): The honest four-category read of the self-hosted AI agent SERP in 2026 — stateful-agent frameworks (Maskin, Letta, Cheshire Cat, Agent Zero, Paperclip), workflow-node builders (n8n, Flowise, Dify, EpicStaff), RAG chat frontends (Open WebUI, LibreChat, AnythingLLM, Bionic GPT), and coding-agent control planes (twelve entrants, covered in a sibling page). Every canonical listicle (Kiebot, Digest.Pro, Lushbinary) mixes the four categories into one flat list; this page runs the split so the buying question is "what is the object of your work?" before "which vendor?" License shape + install shape as load-bearing filters. Category-landing companion to the self-hosted-ai-agent-control-plane page.

## Concepts

- [Core concepts](https://maskin.io/docs/concepts/): Actors (humans and agents), workspaces, the Insights → Bets → Tasks object graph, relationships, comments, triggers, sessions, notifications, skills, files, extensions.
- [Agents & sessions](https://maskin.io/docs/agents/): How agents run — the session lifecycle, logs, token usage, and cost.
- [Architecture](https://maskin.io/docs/architecture/): How the system fits together (server, Postgres, storage, real-time).

## Reference

- [MCP tools](https://maskin.io/docs/mcp-tools/): The full MCP tool surface agents and Claude use to drive a workspace — objects, schema, actors, comments, files, skills, triggers, sessions, notifications, integrations, and LLM keys.
- [API reference](https://maskin.io/docs/api/): The API-first HTTP surface under `/api`, authentication, resource groups, and real-time SSE.
- [OpenAPI spec](https://maskin.io/docs/api/): Each Maskin instance serves a live, authoritative machine-readable API spec at `/openapi.json` (relative to your own instance host, not maskin.io) — point any OpenAPI client or code generator at it.
- [Configuration](https://maskin.io/docs/configuration/): Environment variables and workspace settings.
- [Integrations](https://maskin.io/docs/integrations/): Connect Slack, GitHub, Linear, Gmail, PostHog, and more.
